trust_decision.summary: process_client_headers decides how the client body is framed (Content-Length vs chunked) and then forwards the client's own framing headers to the server. At the pinned commit, when both are present tinyproxy reads the body by Content-Length while the server sees Transfer-Encoding as well. The fix makes chunked win and removes Content-Length.

landing_point.why: The advisory says CL/TE desync, and this is the only line where tinyproxy combines Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding to choose the client body length.

fix_sites.entry_point: Any proxied HTTP request from a client (forward, reverse, transparent, or CONNECT through an HTTP upstream). Reached via handle_connection -> process_client_headers (src/reqs.c:1713).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Anonymous mode is an opt-in header allowlist that the admin configures. The Connection-header token stripping is a separate hop-by-hop feature (it had its own CVE-2023-49606). A non-exact Transfer-Encoding value such as 'gzip, chunked' or a folded header is 'not chunked' to tinyproxy, so a solver could call it unsupported input instead of a CL/TE conflict.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A legitimate request with only Content-Length (POST/PUT) or only Transfer-Encoding: chunked must still be forwarded and streamed. Anonymous mode must still strip unlisted headers. Connection-listed hop-by-hop headers must still be removed. An over-broad fix breaks these: rejecting every request that has a body, forcing TE into the anonymous allowlist without checking it, or refusing all Connection tokens.

O6_input_shapes: Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding: chunked both present (TE matched case-insensitively by is_chunked_transfer, src/reqs.c:824-829)
Several Content-Length headers (pseudomap_remove removes every one, src/pseudomap.c:76-89)

O7_producer.where: src/main.c:341-348 (the anonymous allowlist is built at startup with Content-Length but not Transfer-Encoding). Consumed at src/reqs.c:955-956.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Anonymous mode: the allowlist is auto-extended with Content-Length only. After the fix removes CL from a CL+TE request, TE is also filtered out, so tinyproxy still streams a chunked body to the server with no framing header. A plain chunked request without CL has the same gap at the pinned commit.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Anonymous is an opt-in config feature in another file, and the auto-insert comment talks only about HTTP/1.0 Content-Length.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other file (src/main.c) from the landing point src/reqs.c:920; the effect lands at src/reqs.c:955

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The Connection / Proxy-Connection token removal runs after the framing decision, so a client can list content-length or transfer-encoding as hop-by-hop. The header is then dropped from what is forwarded, while tinyproxy still reads and relays the body by the length it already decided.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Hop-by-hop stripping is a separate RFC feature with its own past CVE fix (src/reqs.c:788-792), not the CL+TE conflict the report describes.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Transfer-Encoding values that are not exactly 'chunked' are treated as not chunked, so tinyproxy frames by CL while forwarding TE to the server. Examples: a list such as 'gzip, chunked', trailing whitespace (chomp strips only CR/LF), an obs-folded value (continuation lines are concatenated with their CRLF), or a second TE header (find returns the first).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Codings other than chunked and folded headers look unsupported or malformed. The fix's own condition calls is_chunked_transfer, so the solver reuses it without asking whether it is right.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; the producers are src/text.c:59-85 (chomp) and src/reqs.c:684-734 (folding in get_all_headers)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Duplicate, conflicting Content-Length headers without TE: tinyproxy uses the first one with atol, and all of them are forwarded to the server.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The report is about CL plus TE, not CL plus CL.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: AddHeader config entries are appended to the client header map before framing is decided, so an AddHeader for Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding feeds the same decision.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Server-response framing: process_server_headers takes content_length.server from CL only and ignores TE (relay stops at src/reqs.c:1221-1223). A CL+TE check could be planted or required here.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same get_content_length helper is used on the response side. A maintainer fixing the request side would plausibly leave the response side alone.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: is_chunked_transfer could be made to parse a comma-separated coding list but only check the first token.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A natural half-fix for the 'gzip, chunked' shape. It sits in the very helper the published fix calls.

O9_family: HTTP request smuggling / message-framing parser differential (CWE-444)

O10_build.toolchain: autotools (autogen.sh/configure/make), gcc; perl for the test scripts
O10_build.project_tests: tests/scripts/run_tests.sh with webserver.pl/webclient.pl: generic perl smoke tests. Nothing specific to CL/TE framing seen.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Make chunked win at src/reqs.c:920 and delete Content-Length (exactly the published fix), without checking the order of the anonymous filter and the Connection-token removal, or the exact-match TE parse.

out_of_scope_notes: After the headers, relay_connection (src/reqs.c:1181-1254) copies raw client bytes to the server for the rest of the connection. The real impact of desync is therefore filter/ACL/auth bypass for a follow-on request, not reaching the backend at all.
